title: Itauma Seeks IBF Heavyweight Crown Against Hrgović at O2 Arena
dek: Moses Itauma, 21, and unbeaten in 14 fights, faces 34-year-old Filip Hrgović for the vacant IBF heavyweight championship at London's O2 Arena on August 29. Itauma would become the second-youngest heavyweight champion in history behind Mike Tyson if he wins.
author: The GoCheckMySports Desk
key_fact: Moses Itauma is 14-0 with 12 knockouts and has boxed only 31 professional rounds; he faces 20-1 Filip Hrgović for the vacant IBF heavyweight title.
bottom_line: Itauma's path to one of sport's highest crowns depends on executing against a veteran opponent with over twice his rounds of experience. Watch how Itauma's uncommon athleticism translates against Hrgović's experience and technique, and whether the young heavyweight's coronation narrative survives contact with a determined spoiler.
body: Moses Itauma, a 21-year-old southpaw from Chatham with an unbeaten professional record, faces Filip Hrgović for the vacant International Boxing Federation heavyweight championship at the O2 Arena in London on August 29. According to Sporting News and Guardian Sport, Itauma's record stands at 14-0 with 12 knockouts, while Hrgović carries a 20-1 record with 15 knockouts.

Itauma would become the second-youngest heavyweight champion of all time behind Mike Tyson if he defeats Hrgović, who is 34 years old. At 21 years and 244 days, per Sporting News, Itauma would also rank as the second-youngest British world champion in history, behind Naseem Hamed.

The challenger from the United Kingdom is characterized by speed uncommon for his size, concussive power, and the ability to attack from unusual angles, according to Guardian Sport. His experience at the elite level remains limited, however, having competed in only 31 professional rounds. Hrgović, a Croatian heavyweight, has frequently dismissed Itauma as a "kid" during the build-up to the bout. At Friday's weigh-in at Spitalfields Market, per Sporting News, Itauma shoved Hrgović off the stage and received a slap in response.

On the undercard, Sam Noakes, 29, from Kent, defeated former world champion Denys Berinchyk by unanimous decision over 10 rounds in a lightweight bout, winning by scores of 100-90, 99-91, and 98-92, according to Sporting News. Noakes described the victory as the biggest win of his career.

Nelson Hysa knocked out Thomas Narmo in round two of a heavyweight bout and called out WBC champion Agit Kabayal ringside after his victory. Constantin Ursu retained the British and Commonwealth welterweight titles against Ben Vaughan. Guido Vianello and Moses Jolly fought to a draw over eight heavyweight rounds. Tony Curtis defeated previously undefeated Imad Naseeb in a six-round super flyweight bout, and Aloys Youmbi faced late replacement Sherif Musah in a cruiserweight contest after Mike Perez withdrew.

The bout is available on DAZN in the UK at 24.99 pounds for the pay-per-view or as part of the DAZN Ultimate subscription at 24.99 pounds monthly. In the United States, PPV pricing is 59.99 dollars, with DAZN Ultimate at 44.99 dollars monthly and a minimum of 12 included pay-per-view events per year.
